images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of Kev-Bio.Qwen3.5 and USFM provide visual tokens to the language model, while DINOv2 contributes additional localization features. Clinical questions are encoded into decision states at⟨decide⟩\langle\mathrm{decide}\rangletokens, which generate queries for each landmark endpoint. A convolutional-based Pixel Neck combines features from the three visual encoders into a shared dense feature map. Endpoint queries are matched against this map to produce spatial probability maps, from which landmark coordinates and clinical measurements are derived.

Figure 2:Qualitative comparison across nine ultrasound views.Landmark predictions from Kev-Bio (red) and US-Foundation (blue), with ground truth shown in green. Values indicate mean landmark error in pixels.

Figure 3:Spatial probability maps and error detection.(a) Landmark probability maps showing confident and ambiguous predictions.
(b) Landmarks are ranked by decreasing map entropy, and curves show the fraction of localization errors captured in each clinical domain. Errors are defined using ground truth as deviations exceeding 5% of the image diagonal. The black marker indicates the overall result, and the dashed line represents random selection.

Figure 4:Question-conditioned landmark localization.Different clinical measurement questions produce distinct landmark probability maps on the same ultrasound image. Green circles denote ground truth, and yellow regions indicate predicted spatial distributions.
